note: Frozen twin case table for pointer-scoped external reference composition. openbindings.openapi@1 section 6 ('Reference scope'): a reference that leaves the current document composes the value at the referenced JSON Pointer together with that value's transitive closure of references, and nothing else. Each case is a multi-document artifact plus the one verdict every engine must reach. The identical file is executed by openbindings-go's formats/openapi, by openapi-client/go, and by openbindings-ts's packages/openapi; a divergence in one fails the others' suites too. Authored from the OAS, JSON Reference and RFC 6901 text; no byte comes from a corpus specimen. ONE case is a disclosed exception to that provenance: 'pointer-below-a-reference' pins a convention of these implementations rather than an authority answer, and its own 'why' says so.

cases.name: defect-outside-the-composed-closure
cases.why: A dangling reference in a component the pointer never reaches is outside the composed closure, so the referencing artifact resolves (openbindings.openapi@1 section 6).

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: defect-inside-the-composed-closure
cases.why: A reference reachable from the referenced pointer, and unresolvable there, does make the referencing artifact unresolvable.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: defect-outside-the-closure-inside-the-same-component
cases.why: The composed value is the value AT the pointer, not the component that contains it: a sibling property of the same Schema Object is outside the closure.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Big/properties/kept"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: target-is-not-an-openapi-document
cases.why: No accepted edition requires a reference target to be a conforming OpenAPI Document; the OAS's own Reference Object examples address a bare schema file.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./fragments.yaml#/Thing"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: pointer-into-a-bare-json-schema-file
cases.why: A JSON Schema resource is a legal reference target; its own $defs are addressable and nothing outside the addressed pointer is composed.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./schema.json#/$defs/Widget"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: cycle-spanning-two-documents
cases.why: A cycle whose members are declared in different documents is composed like any other; both engines must cut it at the same members and name them from the declaring document.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./a.yaml#/components/schemas/Node"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

https://composition.example/a.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: A, version: "1"}
components:
  schemas:
    Node:
      type: object
      properties:
        peer: {$ref: "./b.yaml#/components/schemas/Peer"}

cases.name: relative-base-two-directories-up
cases.why: A relative reference resolves against the referring document's own address, so the closure pass and the resolver must join it the same way.

https://composition.example/spec/v1/open.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "../../shared/library.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: absolute-base-on-another-host
cases.why: An absolute reference identifies its resource without the referring document's base; the same scope rule applies.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "https://library.example/shared.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: target-file-is-not-well-formed
cases.why: Parsing is not scoping: a target that cannot be read as a document fails the reference that reaches it, whatever the pointer would have selected.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./broken.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

https://composition.example/broken.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Broken, version: "1"}
components:
  schemas:
    Used:
      type: array
      items:
      type: integer

cases.name: unreachable-resource-referenced-only-outside-the-closure
cases.why: A resource reached only from outside the composed closure is never retrieved, so its availability cannot decide the artifact.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:

info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:

      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: defect-outside-a-second-hop-closure
cases.why: The closure is transitive: a second document reached through the first composes only what the first reference's value reaches.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./a.yaml#/components/schemas/Used"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

https://composition.example/a.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: A, version: "1"}
components:
  schemas:
    Used:
      type: object
      properties:
        deep: {$ref: "./b.yaml#/components/schemas/Deep"}

cases.name: defect-inside-a-second-hop-closure
cases.why: Transitivity cuts both ways: a defect the second hop's value does reach refuses the artifact.

info: {title: A, version: "1"}

cases.name: pointer-below-a-reference
cases.why: CONVENTION, NOT AUTHORITY. Both engines reach a position that lies below a reference, and no authority decides whether they should: RFC 6901 section 4 evaluates each token against the document's contents, under which 'Alias/properties/name' denotes nothing, while JSON Reference section 4 says an implementation MAY replace a reference with the referenced value, after which it denotes the string. Neither text sequences the two. Both engines did this before pointer scope was implemented and the block preserved it rather than smuggle a new observable behavior in under a conformance fix. Pinned here so the two engines cannot drift apart while the question is open; recorded as an open item in corpus-lab/OPENAPI-RUNTIME.md.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Alias/properties/name"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: whole-file-reference-composes-the-file
cases.why: A reference with no fragment addresses the resource root, so the composed value is the whole file and a defect anywhere in it is inside the closure.

cases.name: defect-in-a-sibling-sequence-element
cases.why: A sequence member is addressed by index exactly as an object member is addressed by name: the composed value is allOf/0, so the defective allOf/1 beside it is outside the closure and the referencing artifact resolves.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Combo/allOf/0"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

cases.name: two-pointers-into-one-sequence
cases.why: Two references compose two elements of the same sequence, and the element between them - which nothing composes and which is defective - is outside the closure. allOf/2 must still denote the third element, so no index may be renumbered.

https://composition.example/openapi.yaml.text:
openapi: 3.1.2
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Combo/allOf/0"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}
  /others:
    post:
      operationId: createOther
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Combo/allOf/2"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}
